blocks.text: You can specify whether device information (i.e., device hostname, device owner, and device name) are visible or obfuscated for an admin when they view dashboards, reports, or insights.
If admins need to view device information, they must have an auditor grant them permission to do so. To learn more, see About Auditors.
To configure this setting for an admin account, your own admin account must meet the following conditions:

blocks.item: Your admin account must have an admin role that has Full permission to Administrators Access. To learn more, see Adding Admin Roles.
Your admin account must have organizational admin scope. To learn more, see About Admin Scope.
If your organization has the admin rank feature enabled, and you're configuring this setting for another admin account, that admin must have an admin rank lower than or equal to your own admin rank.

blocks.text: To obfuscate device information for an admin viewing dashboards, reports, and insights, you must enable device information obfuscation for the role assigned to the admin. In other words, you must edit the admin role assigned to the admin account or create an new role.
To obfuscate device information for an admin, do one of the following:

blocks.item: Assign the admin an existing role with device information obfuscation enabled.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Role Management > Internet & SaaS.
Ensure that you have a role with the appropriate permissions for the admin you want to assign the role to and that the Device Information column for that row displays Obfuscated.
Go to Administration > Role Management > Administrative Entitlements.
Select Zscaler Internet Access.
See image.
Select the Users tab.
Click Assign Users.
The Select Users & Roles page appears.
On the Select Users & Roles page, select the admins you want to enable obfuscation for and select the role that has obfuscation enabled from the drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
Activate the change.
Enable device information obfuscation for an existing role.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Legacy Admin Management > Internet & SaaS.

On the Administrators tab, in the Role column, check which admin role is assigned to the admin you want to edit. Also, check which other admins have been assigned this specific role, and ensure you want device information obfuscation enabled for those admins as well.
See image.
Go to Administration > Role Management > Internet & SaaS.
Click the Edit icon for the role assigned to the admin you're editing.
The Edit Administrator Role window appears.
In the Edit Administrator Role window, For Device Information, choose Obfuscated.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
Add a new role with device information obfuscation enabled and assign it to the admin.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Role Management > Internet & SaaS.
Click Add Administrator Role.
The Add Administrator Role window appears.
In the Add Administrator Role window, follow the instructions for adding a new admin role, including how to enable device information obfuscation.
Go to Administration > Role Management > Administrative Entitlements.
Select Zscaler Internet Access.
See image.
Select the Users tab.
Click Assign Users.
The Select Users & Roles page appears.
On the Select Users & Roles page, select the admins you want to enable obfuscation for and select the role that has obfuscation enabled from the drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
Activate the change.
Add a new admin role and account.
For convenience, Zscaler recommends creating the admin role first so you can assign the role to the new admin.
Add a new admin role with device information obfuscation enabled.
Add a new user.
Assign an administrative entitlement for Zscaler Internet Access to the user with the newly created role selected.
